text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower on Monday with activity centered on book-squaring ahead of the expiry of spot position May. The May/August spread narrowed to $2.00 by the close from Friday's $3.30 finish as some players rolled forward the May position before the April 15 expiry.

By the close, May stood $1.00 down at $309.90 per tonne and August 20 cents lower at $307.90 per tonne. Traders noted little arbitrage activity against the New York raws market. May/May was valued at around $67 per tonne, slightly narrower than on Friday.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended unchanged for the third consecutive session after setting an eight-point trading range early and then drifting within narrow boundaries throughout the day. May closed at 11.00 cents/lb, having ranged from 11.03 to 10.95 cents. Deferreds settled 0.02 higher to 0.01 weaker. Support remained at the recent low of 10.78 cents basis May.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports in January 1997 reached 354,749 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 137,215 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 833,115 tonnes compared to 443,279 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 2.615 mn tonnes compared to 1.557 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/January 1996/97 were Brazil with 108,102 tonnes raws against 77,223 tonnes, the Philippines with 98,033 tonnes compared to nil, Colombia with 88,193 tonnes, up from 48,782 tonnes and Australia with 63,311 tonnes compared to 30,000 tonnes.

The largest white sugar supplier in October/January 1996/97 was Canada with 14,274 tonnes compared to 23,627 tonnes followed by Mexico with 12,920 tonnes against 6 tonnes. Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 17,448 tonnes, down from 28,596 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/January 1996/97 up to 67,776 tonnes against 132,941 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 310,341 tonnes, down from 504,854 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/January 1996/97 were Jamaica with 12,386 tonnes whites against 13,934 tonnes, Haiti with 11,076 tonnes compared to 13,593 tonnes and Peru with 8,414 tonnes compared to 15,887 tonnes.

MAURITIUS - Sugar exports in December 1996 reached 74,603 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 70,044 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (June/December) up to 487,498 tonnes, sharply up on last year's 403,831 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 565,608 tonnes against 525,697 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in June/December 1996 were the UK with 361,607 tonnes raws against 352,511 tonnes, Portugal with 83,104 tonnes, up from 19,080 tonnes and the USA with 24,180 tonnes, up from 2,187 tonnes.

Sugar output in 1996/97 reached 623,880 tonnes, down from 646,200 tonnes estimated earlier, but still up on the cyclone reduced 1995/96 result of 571,515 tonnes. Due to lower than expected production and heavy export commitments Mauritius is forced import sugar with total shipments in June/December 1996 amounting to 15,920 tonnes compared to 21,135 tonnes in the like period the previous year. The only country of origin in June/December 1996 was South Africa.

Libya last week purchased between four and five cargoes of white sugar for April/June shipment, traders recently said. The prices paid were between $360 and $365 a tonne, they said. Libya entered the market last month to buy white sugar but postponed its tender at least once.
